Level
Storage

Backup speedMax
Applies to export and restore. Try a lower setting if backups fail.
Video decoding
Native video player (beta)
Plays video with Android's own player for smoother playback and less battery. Filters, zoom, motion smoothing, upscaling and the Bluetooth delay all run natively on the GPU. The app reloads to switch.
Play anything with the VLC engine
When a file or stream won't play here (WMV, RealMedia, DTS soundtracks, odd AVIs, RTSP/MMS streams, network shares), hand it to the built-in VLC engine instead. Audio is converted once and keeps the EQ and effects; video opens in a full-screen VLC player.
Frame-drop protection
Reduces effects to keep video smooth. Auto: only when a video starts skipping frames. Light: always.
Audio lead (no frame drops)
Plays the sound ahead of the video instead of delaying the picture, so video never drops frames. The visualizer is silent on video while this is on.
Lossless latency (no dropped frames)
Fixes videos losing frames while the latency delay is on.
Delayed picture sharpness
Picture sharpness while the delay is on. Low is lightest but soft; High is sharper and uses more memory.
Lighten UI while video plays
Freezes animated backgrounds while a video plays to prevent dropped frames. They return when paused.

Audio quality and decoding

        

          

            
Hi-res output

            
Plays 24-bit and 32-bit files (and lossless Dolby TrueHD / DTS-HD soundtracks) at full depth, as 32-bit float, instead of 16-bit. The equalizer, effects, volume boost, ReplayGain, speed, pitch and the visualizer all keep working on them, at full depth too. Other files are not affected.

          

          
        

        

          

            
Upconvert 16-bit audio

            
Plays 16-bit music and video soundtracks (most MP3, AAC and CD rips) at 32-bit float while they play, so the equalizer, bass, boost and effects work with headroom and full precision instead of being squeezed back into 16 bits, which is what makes heavy settings crackle. Your files are not changed. Turns on Hi-res output for 24-bit files too.

          

          
        

        

          

            
Save a high bit depth copy

            
Makes a permanent WAV copy of the playing song at 24-bit or 32-bit float and adds it to your library. It sounds the same as the original (the extra bits start out empty) and is much bigger: about 15 MB a minute at 24-bit, 20 MB at 32-bit. For smoother effects, Upconvert 16-bit audio above does the same job without the big file.

            

          

          

            
            
          

        

        

          

            
Audio decoder

            
Auto uses the best decoder for each file. Software only and Hardware only force that kind and nothing else, so nothing switches behind your back. Most phones decode music in software, so with Hardware only many files stay silent; Software only includes the built-in Dolby / DTS decoders.

          

          
        

        

          

            
Video decoder

            
For the native video player. Software only is slower and uses more battery, but can fix a video that stutters or shows a broken picture. Hardware only never falls back to software: a video the phone's chip cannot decode will not play.
